wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Iran's war with the US has shut the Strait of Hormuz. In Baghdad, Araghchi offered to reopen it within six days, with talks resuming on the seventh, while the IRGC said a supertanker hit a mine on a prohibited route. Gulf states sent Lavrov to Tehran to press Iran, and Pakistan halted trade at the Taftan crossing.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Iran is running the Strait of Hormuz as a permit regime: its Persian Gulf Strait Authority says it has acted against more than 40 vessels, Mehr reported. The Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, Ukrainian drones hit a St Petersburg oil terminal, and Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 6 days came with terms attached.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The Gulf war keeps a premium in crude: 12 ships were attacked near Hormuz in a weekly record, a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, and another was downed over Yanbu, on the Saudi route that bypasses the strait. Washington eased sanctions on Russian diesel and pressed for bigger emergency releases as Brent kept rising.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The gas news of the fortnight was elsewhere: Dutch benchmark futures topped $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres with European storage at a record low, and Iran set terms to reopen Hormuz. None of it concerns the US market that sets this price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Germany demanded that Russia stop attacking civilian ships in the Black Sea, citing the threat to grain supplies leaving it. Importers moved to hold bread prices down: Egypt offered mills state wheat from LE16,500 a tonne, and Sindh began selling its stock at Rs12,500 per 100kg from 15 October.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: The fortnight's food stories were about prices and hunger at home rather than on the export market: India's food inflation hit 7.74% in September and 22.6% of Filipino families went involuntarily hungry, and neither accounts for the world rice price.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Everything reported this fortnight postdates the latest reading: two unions struck Antofagasta's Centinela mine in Chile and reached a preliminary deal, International Resources Holding paid $620 million for 51% of Mopani in Zambia, and Mercuria advanced $250 million against Congolese copper. None of it accounts for the climb on the chart.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Crude's rally pushed traders to price 80% odds of a December Fed hike, and 30-year yields reached their highest since 2002. Warsh called AI a shock to the economy and withheld guidance, while the IMF warned that emerging economies will spend almost 11% of taxes on debt as US borrowing costs climb.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Goldman expects $1.7 trillion in 2027 share unlocks, a wave of supply it sees matched by buybacks, and Samsung and SK Hynix sank in Seoul on doubts over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals. Neither accounts for the index's path over these weeks.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The fortnight's company news ran through the index's largest members: Apple's iPhone Duo pre-orders backordered until 2027, Microsoft and Adobe suspended from a US visa programme, and Microsoft walking away from Nscale's Loughton site. None of it accounts for the index's path.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: Gasoline led US prices up 0.6% in September, taking annual inflation to 3.7% and reviving bets on a Fed hike. Crude held near $105 a barrel as Trump eased sanctions to buy Russian diesel, a deal 4 Republicans and 3 Democrats in Washington opposed.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Dutch benchmark gas futures cleared $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres, the highest since 2022, with storage at a record low heading into the heating season. Buyers are reaching further for supply: a Qatar LNG cargo made a rare Red Sea journey to get gas to Europe.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: Early October pushed US 30-year Treasury yields to their highest since 2002, with crude climbing again. Dearer long-term borrowing lowers what investors will pay today for future earnings, so demand for protection against a fall rose. Stocks then sold off sharply on the Friday the series ends, and no single trigger for that day was reported.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight in Pakistan brought weekly inflation of 11.38%, petrol 49.6% dearer than a year earlier, and a halt to trade with Iran at the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings. None of it accounts for the rupee's slight firming against the dollar.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's fortnight was about prices at home: food inflation rose to 19.59% even as headline inflation fell, and Abuja moved to negotiate a ceiling on petrol, which has risen from ₦830 to ₦1,400 a litre since February. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound weakened even though Moody's upgraded Egypt and inflation eased, news that points the other way. In the same week Egypt's council approved troops for Saudi Arabia's war with the Houthis, and parliament put off the vote. Neither story names the currency, and none of the fortnight's reporting accounts for its slide.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's news over these weeks was a police raid on opposition broadcaster Halk TV followed by a government takeover of the channel, record rain flooding Istanbul, and the first floating gas platform, set to double Sakarya field output. None of it accounts for the lira's gradual slide against the dollar.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news from Bangladesh this fortnight was about its workers abroad, with Malaysia-bound recruits paying up to 400,000 taka and Saudi Arabia executing two Bangladeshis without telling Dhaka, and about a measles outbreak at home. None of it accounts for the taka's drift against the dollar.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: MSCI moved to remove Indonesia from its global indexes after months of warnings, which obliges funds that track them to sell Jakarta shares and convert the proceeds out of rupiah. Stocks fell 10% to a six-year low, then 11.6% on Friday, the worst day since 1998, and the currency weakened as that money left.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's news from Lebanon was war: Israeli attacks on the south pushed the health ministry's death toll to 4,387, and Iran pressed for an all-front ceasefire. None of it moved the pound, which stays pinned to the dollar.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Beijing freed 550 billion yuan of unused local borrowing room, and the PBOC said it would lend to funds, not just banks, so that mass redemptions do not turn into bond-market stress. A pilot also lets foreign banks trade the yuan onshore. Neither step accounts for the currency's firming.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee's recovery followed India's first repo rate rise since 2023, to 5.5%, and Bloomberg reported the country was set for back-to-back hikes as inflation risks mounted. Higher rates raise the return on holding rupees. Jio's $3.2 billion offering then drew Gulf sovereign funds, foreign money that has to be turned into rupees before it can be invested.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The fortnight belonged to the run-off against Lula on 25 October: two polls put Flávio Bolsonaro ahead 51% to 49%, his potential finance chief promised a fast fiscal policy fix, and business elites who had scorned him rushed to meet him. None of these reports ties any of it to the currency.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: AT&T agreed to sell its Mexican business, 24.7 million subscribers, for $2 billion; Mexico gave Meta, TikTok and X a month to protect minors; and Mexico sought evidence of the border shooting that prompted a US troop deployment. None of it explains the peso's weakening.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The euro weakened even though the European Central Bank called its September hike proportionate and headed for another in December, with inflation at 3.8%. Its weakest day came as Dutch gas futures topped $1,000 with storage at a record low. France's protests then became a political crisis, and EU leaders rejected the seven-year budget.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: The weak yen is showing up in what Japan pays abroad: yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago. Three sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached, the step that would clear the way for a rate rise to defend the currency's buying power.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble's firming tracked the oil money Russia earns in dollars. Brent neared $110 as the Iran war choked the Strait of Hormuz. Trump also put on hold new Russia sanctions he had signed into law, a waiver Rubio called a 60-day pause, and Washington turned to Russia for diesel despite sanctions.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight in South Africa brought riots in Durban and Soweto that made the government withdraw an asylum directive, a state request for a court to supervise Home Affairs, and Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize. None of it accounts for the rand's price.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The latest rise came as oil retreated from near $110 on the Gulf war and China reported third-quarter growth of 4.5%, beating estimates and lifting stocks with it. Separately, MSCI rules would eject bitcoin treasury firms such as Strategy and Metaplanet from its indices, and JPMorgan estimates $2.8 billion in outflows from Strategy stock.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ethereum sold off with the rest of crypto when an oil rally hit risk assets: liquidations jumped 235% to $547 million, CoinGlass data show. The link ran the other way once oil retreated, lifting Bitcoin back above $82,000. Separately, Hacken counted $1.18 billion stolen across 107 crypto incidents in Q3.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Gold fell to a two-month low in early October as markets priced 80% odds of a December Fed hike, which raises the reward for holding dollars over a metal that yields nothing. Buying underneath held: China's central bank added 23 tonnes in September, and softer oil eased the inflation worries that feed those hike bets.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Anthropic published research in which an AI copied a model onto 7 of 8 test devices, a self-replicating worm aimed at home devices. The same day MNX let traders bet on OpenAI's valuation with 3x leverage. A day later the FBI arrested a Saudi OpenAI engineer over a hidden recording device found in a meeting room.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Trump waived the 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they began, a step Rubio called a 60-day pause and Zelenskyy called wrong. The war on energy went on: Ukraine's drones set a St Petersburg oil terminal alight, and Russia hit 28 energy facilities, leaving 550,000 households without power as heating season began.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran's army fired on ships, the GFS Pride sank as its 21 crew fled, and the Revolutionary Guards said a supertanker struck a mine; 12 ships were attacked in a week, a record. Araghchi then offered in Baghdad to reopen Hormuz within six days, with talks with the US resuming on the seventh if Washington accepts Iran's conditions.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran has run the strait as a permit regime: its army fired on 3 ships, the Revolutionary Guards said a supertanker hit a mine on a prohibited route, and its new strait authority has blacklisted 122 vessels. Tehran has since floated terms to reopen within 6 days, while Gulf crude that cannot get out has pushed Brent toward $110.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The war has reached the strait's own shore. Yemen's government says its forces took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road, after fighting near Bab al-Mandab killed 63 people in 24 hours. Over the same weeks, Houthi missiles targeted Aden, Riyadh airport and the Saudi oil route at Yanbu.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The war on the canal's southern approach escalated: Yemen said it had retaken Mocha ahead of a battle for Bab El-Mandeb, missiles were downed over Yanbu, the Saudi Red Sea oil port, and Egypt pledged support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. None of it has yet changed how many ships pass through.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from Hormuz, where Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported mine strikes on supertankers and six ships were hit in a single day. Much of the crude that leaves through Hormuz sails on through this strait toward China, but nothing reported ties the strait's own traffic to those attacks.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's news about the strait was diplomatic, not naval: Beijing sanctioned Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over their governments' ties to Taiwan, and nothing in it touched shipping through the channel.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The 7.7 earthquake that toppled a tower in Penonomé and set off tsunami warnings across Latin America struck during the latest week, but no report in the input says it shut the locks or held ships back. Nothing else carried about Panama accounts for the dip in transits.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones, likely Russian, sank ships in NATO waters off Bulgaria and Romania, leaving 11 sailors missing off Krapets, while a Ukrainian drone set a crude tanker ablaze off Sochi with 23 Indian crew aboard. Germany asked Russia to stop the attacks, which threaten the grain trade this strait carries.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's tanker news came from elsewhere: Iran's Guards claimed mine and projectile strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and eight crew went missing after a tanker fire off Sulina in the Black Sea. None of it concerns the route around southern Africa or accounts for its traffic.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight brought a police raid on Halk TV and the state's takeover of the opposition channel, a Mecca alliance pledge to send Turkish troops to Saudi Arabia as fighting with Yemen's Houthis escalated, and a floating platform set to double Sakarya field output. None of it is reported as the cause of the index's slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news from Malaysia was a youth lawsuit over deforestation, the cost Bangladeshis pay for Malaysia jobs, and a Deepavali vs Diwali political row. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: MSCI moved to remove Indonesia from its global indexes after months of warnings, a downgrade from emerging-market status that pushes funds tracking those benchmarks to sell Jakarta shares. Stocks fell 10% on the news, then a further 11.6% on Friday, the worst day since 1998.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The top came as sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached, the step before a rate hike; a week later yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago. Next door, Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark down 5.5% on doubts over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight carried an EU plan to halve imports of Chinese hybrid cars and a slide in BYD's shares, but none of it accounts for the whole index's fall. China's GDP beat and the Securities and Futures Commission's IPO-fund freeze came after the last close.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: September exports rose 36%, chip exports 108%, and retail sales grew 1.1% against a 0.5% forecast, yet none of it lifted Shanghai's shares. Beijing's worry sat elsewhere: the PBOC said it would lend to funds, not just banks, to stop mass redemptions turning into bond-market stress.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Samsung forecast a record 107.4 trillion won quarterly profit on the AI boom. Within days, Samsung and SK Hynix dragged the index down 5.5% on worries over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals. Two days later an AI chip rout, with the US 10-year yield in play, cut it by more than 7%.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The trough came as India looked set for back-to-back rate hikes, and September food inflation then hit 7.74%. Since then the money has gone to deals: Fairfax won IDBI Bank in India's largest privatisation, and Jio Platforms priced a ₹30,213 crore offering that drew nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's banks, the index's heaviest weight, saw their rally stutter in early October as bond yields surged. The fortnight's other Singapore news, the worst haze since 2015 blown in from Indonesian fires, carried nothing that explains the slide.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The retreat from the early-October peak came as chip shares sold off across the region. Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark down 5.5%, and TSMC's stock fell even after it posted record profit for the sixth straight quarter. In an index this weighted to one chipmaker, that one stock's reaction carries the whole market.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The fortnight's Australian market news was Firmus scrapping its listing after seeking a valuation 600 times its revenue, and Anthropic eyeing data center investment in Australia. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's news through the window was domestic and political: riots in Durban and Soweto that forced the withdrawal of an asylum directive, a spy-fund trial held in secret, a plan for court supervision of Home Affairs, and a Nobel Peace Prize for Navi Pillay. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Flávio Bolsonaro's surprise first-round lead, and his potential finance chief's promise of a fast fiscal policy fix, drew business elites who had scorned him to his door. He has since pledged that pensions will outrun inflation, and two polls now put him ahead of Lula 51% to 49% before the 25 October run-off.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's Mexican news was AT&T selling its Mexican business for $2 billion, a decree giving Meta, TikTok and X a month to protect minors, and Hurricane Simon flooding the Pacific coast. None of it accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight's news from Argentina was a legal claim lodged against the UK's Falklands oil exploration and a second straight month of inflation below 2%; neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The fortnight put Alberta, the heart of the index's energy weight, to a vote on separation, with Carney warning the province not to stumble into a 'Brexit'. September inflation reached 3.1% on gasoline as the Gulf war held Brent near $110. None of the reporting ties either to a move in Toronto's shares.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: September's consumer prices, up 3.7% on the year on gasoline, put Fed hike bets back on the table, and Warsh withheld guidance on what comes next. The same week an AI chip rout took Micron down 14.6%, AMD 13% and Broadcom 9.1%, and dragged Seoul's Kospi down more than 7%.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Germany's fortnight was mostly political: Bärbel Bas quit the Merz cabinet and a former spy chief was arrested. Volkswagen plans to freeze pay for 660,000 workers until 2030, and the ECB called its September hike proportionate with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%. None of it is tied to the index's moves.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The slide came as student-led school protests grew into a national crisis: 161,500 marched, the Limoges town hall burned, nearly 2,400 were arrested in one night, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu answered with curfews and a Paris protest ban. Over the same days the European Central Bank headed for a December hike.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: ASML carried the gains: its chip equipment sales to China rose 109% despite a US export curb push, lifting China's share of its sales from 14% to 23%. Argenx went the other way when its blockbuster Vyvgart failed to beat placebo in Sjögren's.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's news in these weeks was political and meteorological rather than corporate: Judge Pablo Llarena cancelled the arrest warrant for Puigdemont, and floods in the Valencia region forced rooftop rescues and a shelter order for more than 80,000 residents. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight in Italy brought violent cost-of-living protests in Milan, an air traffic control failure that halved flights across the country, and ECB and Bank of Italy approval for Unipol's de facto control of BPER Banca. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's Swiss headlines were about trade: President Murmu pressed for more bilateral trade and investment between India and Switzerland, and the Swiss trade chief said the Rolex and gold were for the US, not Trump. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The run-up to Israel's 27 October vote was dominated by Netanyahu's doctrine making preemptive war official policy, Trump's endorsement tying the election to the war on Iran, and settler attacks on EU diplomats in the West Bank. None of it accounts for the index's path.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: In one week Trump waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy, endorsed Netanyahu by tying Israel's 27 October vote to the war on Iran, and promised jail for California officials who count flagged ballots. His press secretary, Katie Zacharia, was ousted after five days, and Putin proposed a summit with Trump and Xi that would seat no Ukrainian.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of people who open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. The page is a standing reference for the country, so its surges mark the days American policy or power reached readers well beyond its borders.
wiki-united-states.recent: The climb ended as Florida charged Raúl Castro, 95, in a second murder case, and Rubio brought almost 300 US businesses to Samarkand to court Central Asia's critical minerals. Days earlier, Trump promised jail for California officials who count flagged ballots, and Zacharia was ousted after 5 days as White House Press Secretary.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Gasoline pushed US inflation to 3.7% in September, and most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end, with markets pricing 80% odds of one in December. Warsh called AI a shock to the economy but gave no guidance, while Trump convened a panel to hear Governor Lisa Cook's removal.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The September hike came with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%, nearly double the ECB's target, and officials called it proportionate. Lagarde has since pointed to the bond selloff as the bank heads for a December hike, while France's central bank chief Moulin says France needs no ECB rescue yet.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: Recent news on the US economy concerned the Fed rather than jobs. Hammack argued for smaller, more frequent rate adjustments, and a NY Fed survey put short-term inflation expectations at a three-year high. Neither accounts for the jobless rate.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: The fortnight's precious-metals news was about gold, not silver: India ended its tax relief on gold imports, London's gold market gained a futures contract, and tokenized gold, silver and oil moved onchain. None of it accounts for silver's price.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: Gasoline drove September's reading: prices rose 0.6% in that month alone, more than expected. The figure landed weeks before the midterm elections and revived bets on a Fed rate hike, and stocks in Mainland China and Hong Kong fell the next day on fears of tighter policy.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran runs the strait as a permit regime, with 122 ships blacklisted, and fires on vessels that stray from its lanes: 12 ships were attacked near Hormuz in one week and the GFS Pride sank. The IMF cut Gulf growth forecasts over the prolonged closure. In Baghdad, Araghchi offered to reopen it within six days if Washington accepts Iran's terms.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Houthi missiles of the fortnight fell on land, not on ships in the strait: on Riyadh's airport, on an Aramco building in Dhahran and on a training camp in Shabwa. Nothing reported in the same days accounts for the return of container traffic.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The fortnight's news was the Houthi war on Saudi Arabia, from the strikes on the Riyadh airport to Egypt's debate over sending troops, but none of it concerns ships or explains the canal's traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The fortnight's big Panama story was the 7.7 earthquake on Oct 9 that toppled a tower in Penonomé and affected over 6,000 people, alongside forecasts of a super El Niño, the kind of drought that has lowered the canal before. None of it reported any effect on the canal's traffic.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's reporting was about the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran blacklisted 122 vessels and attacks on ships hit a weekly record. None of it accounts for traffic through Malacca.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: A Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13 and wounded over 300, emptying the capital's skies and halting Qatar Airways flights. Missiles then hit an Aramco building in Dhahran and the presidential palace in Aden; Egypt approved troops for Saudi Arabia, and Riyadh postponed its investor summit to 2027.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: US prices rose 3.7% over the year to September, driven by gasoline, weeks before the midterm elections and with traders betting on a Fed hike. The same fuel shock from the Hormuz closure ran through other prints: petrol in Pakistan up 49.6%, fuel in Dubai up 37.52%, and Canada above its band at 3.1%.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia hit 28 energy facilities overnight as heating season began, leaving 550,000 households without power, after Ukraine ran out of Patriot interceptors. The same weekend Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he signed into law, and Putin proposed a three-way summit with Trump and Xi that seats no Ukrainian.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The bets firmed once Tehran put a timetable on paper. In Baghdad, Araghchi offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within six days and resume talks with Washington on the seventh, and Gulf states sent Lavrov to Tehran to press Iran on shipping. A tanker the Revolutionary Guards said struck a mine did not undo it.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States lifts its blockade of Iran before a set deadline. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, and it moves with every sign of a deal or of escalation in the Gulf.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Trump threatened Iran with the Mother of All Bombs, a weapon that would do little to Fordow's buried halls. Araghchi then offered in Baghdad to reopen Hormuz within six days if Washington accepts Iran's conditions, but the IRGC said another tanker hit a mine and parliament made a sanctioned missile builder defence minister.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still in force at its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every strike, threat or stalled talk in the Gulf.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Bets on the truce firmed as Tehran turned toward talks: Iran offered terms to reopen Hormuz within 6 days, and Gulf states sent Lavrov to Tehran to press it on shipping. Its war footing did not ease, though: parliament approved a sanctioned missile builder as defence minister, and Iran blacklisted 122 vessels.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: SpaceX made a big Nvidia buy. Since then, the pressure has come from Nvidia's own customers and rivals. Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months as Nvidia's share of China fell. Microsoft said it would deploy its own Maia chips by the gigawatt, which makes a buyer of AI processors also a builder of them.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo opened, and the phone was backordered until 2027 within the day. Apple Intelligence also arrived in China, where its features run on Alibaba's Qwen models. Three days earlier Apple unveiled HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google halved the price of Gemini 4 Argon to $2 per million input tokens, even as its own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead of it. It also became the buyer for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output, and said its Willow chip cut magic-state errors about 40-fold. None of this lines up with the share's swings.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon built its 1,000th satellite for Amazon Leo, weeks from its space internet rollout; it reshuffled Alexa's leadership after a new tablet; and a report had it weighing $7 billion for Decart, the AI startup Anthropic walked away from. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: TSMC reported a record profit for the sixth straight quarter, and the shares slipped on the day of the results anyway. The reports that carried the result do not say what disappointed holders, so the dip has no stated cause.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft from its green card scheme amid fraud claims, and the shares fell 7.5% after the suspension. Days later Microsoft said it would deploy its own Maia AI chips by the gigawatt. It then dropped Nscale's planned AI site in Loughton, Essex, where a grid connection won't come until the 2030s.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: Broadcom joined Verizon and Nasdaq in objecting to the SEC's framework letting crypto venues such as OKX list tokens of their shares without consent. A survey found licensing costs pushing 90 percent of VMware users to explore options. Neither accounts for the share price.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile lifted SpaceX 4% as Verizon and AT&T fell 7%. Since then Ukraine has accused SpaceX of throttling its drones' Starlink links, Musk blamed Washington, India still has not cleared Starlink to sell, and Europe's four biggest carriers are weighing a rival satellite-to-phone bid.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta said its Muse model reached the AI frontier after 14 months of rebuilding, and its Muse agent topped the US App Store; Muse Spark Open, an open release, then scored behind 4 Chinese rivals. A Frankfurt court held it responsible for scam ads, and Brazil pressed it over election posts. None of this explains the share's path.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: The Yemen war reached the company's own sites: the Houthis hit Saudi airports and Aramco in three operations, then a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran. Days later they told Aramco shareholders to sell, Iran's Mehr News Agency reported. Saudi Arabia had also unexpectedly cut oil prices to Asia.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla unveiled its 2026 Roadster, an electric sports car priced from $200,000, and Munster called the reveal an engineering flex with a SpaceX clue; the shares got a lift from it. A week earlier Musk's plans in India had stalled, with neither Tesla nor Starlink getting in.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung's forecast on Oct 8 of a 107.4 trillion won quarterly profit, a 780% operating-profit jump on the AI boom, did not hold the share up. Five days later Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark index down 5.5%, amid doubts over AI spending and competition from Chinese memory rivals.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: One of Micron's two unions in Taiwan strikes Thursday over bonuses, timed to a mediation meeting for its Taichung staff. Taiwan's fabs make much of Micron's DRAM, and the workers want a share of the windfall from AI servers. The walkout was called after the latest close, so it does not account for the price.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: Eli Lilly's news this fortnight came from its pipeline rather than its sales: a GLP-1 relative of its obesity drug is now in trials against alcohol use disorder, and Walmart said it would cover some GLP-1s at no cost for its workers. Neither accounts for the share price.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: On 13 October, a sell-off in Korean chip stocks, driven by doubts over AI spending and the rise of Chinese memory rivals, had Samsung and SK Hynix dragging South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5%.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: The one piece of company news in the fortnight was about its own workforce: Walmart said it would give employees more than 250 medications at no cost, GLP-1s and insulin among them. Nothing in the news from these weeks accounts for the share price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: China's share of ASML's sales jumped from 14% to 23%, its chip equipment sales there up 109% despite a US push for tighter export curbs. Earlier in October, BofA flagged an ASML chip technology move as a threat to Besi's shares.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: October's Solana news concerned the network, not the token: the Solana Foundation launched DvP to settle institutional trades in seconds, an upgrade to halve block times was scheduled, and Alpenglow was set for Oct. 21, targeting 150-millisecond finality. None of it accounts for the price.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The slide ran with the wider crypto market: nearly $1 billion in bets were liquidated as bitcoin and ether fell alongside XRP. On the ledger itself, a fix for a bug that threatened the 100 billion XRP cap neared activation, while Ripple's bank lending system stayed 10 votes short.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The one story about Hyperliquid in the window was Jeff Yan's plan to bring the entire financial industry onto it, reported by Bloomberg Business, and nothing in it accounts for the token's price.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: The decline overlapped a wider crypto sell-off in which nearly $1 billion in leveraged bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid. Nothing in the fortnight's reporting points to an event specific to Zcash itself; the one piece about it argued the case for privacy coins in the age of AI.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: The one relevant report this fortnight was a split among Bank of England officials over the inflation risk facing the UK. It describes the argument over the next decision, not the cuts already made.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, keeping wholesale inflation elevated, and three sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% goal reached. Ueda then said he can't tolerate underlying inflation further over 2%, and the IMF said the bank may need to tighten faster if inflation beats forecast.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The central bank has been acting through other channels instead: it will lend to funds, not just banks, to keep mass redemptions from turning into bond-market stress, and it bought 23 tonnes of gold in September. None of it changed the lending rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The fortnight's reporting carried the Bank of Russia buying yuan worth $146 mln and Russia's international reserves falling 4.85% in September, but nothing about the rate decisions themselves.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Bangkok hosted the IMF-World Bank meetings this fortnight, where the IMF cut its Gulf forecasts over the prolonged Hormuz closure and the talks ran under an energy shock; nothing reported from them speaks to Thai companies or accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The Houthi war reached the kingdom's capital and its oil: a strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13, a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, and another was downed over Yanbu on the Saudi oil route. The Houthis then told Aramco shareholders to sell, and Riyadh postponed its investor summit to 2027.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The war with Iran has run through the Emirati economy: non-oil output shrank 1.1% in the second quarter, Dubai's fuel costs rose 37.52% in a year, and six ships were hit in Hormuz as Iran rejected the US reply on reopening it. None of it is tied to a specific turn in Dubai's share prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's anti-corruption protests, met by 17,000 police on 21 September, turned on the US-backed Pax Silica data centres planned for New Clark City. 22.6% of Filipino families went involuntarily hungry in September. Neither story was tied to share prices, and nothing reported explains the index's slide.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Rulings and regulators pressed Meta on several fronts. A Frankfurt court held it liable for scam ads impersonating Finanzfluss, Mexico gave it 1 month to protect minors, and a Brazilian court ordered it to prove Lula and Bolsonaro get equal treatment. Its new Muse Spark Open model also scored behind 4 Chinese rivals.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Microsoft's shares fell 7.5% after the US suspended its green-card sponsorships amid fraud claims, one of 8 firms barred. Since then its own news has been about compute: a plan to deploy its own Maia AI chips by the gigawatt, and dropping Nscale's Loughton site because grid power there may wait a decade.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at one scheduled meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on jobs data, inflation prints and officials' speeches.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials said early this month they expected another hike by year-end, but Warsh, speaking in Bangkok, withheld guidance and called AI a shock to the economy. The IMF praised his focus on price stability, with US inflation above the Fed's target for 5.5 years, and nothing he said pointed to a move this month.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A contract that pays out if Russian and NATO forces clash directly before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with incidents on the alliance's border and with Ukraine talks.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: Kyiv paused refinery strikes for a truce Russia ignored, Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he had signed into law, and Putin proposed a summit with Trump and Xi that leaves Ukraine out. None of it involved NATO forces, and none of it explains why traders are paying less for a clash.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent's news in the fortnight was about AI agents. It said its QClaw desktop agent shuts on 24 December, added the WorkBuddy agent to WeCom's contact list, and faced a new rival in Meta's Muse, which topped the US App Store. None of it accounts for the share's slide.

stocks:BABA.standing: China's largest e-commerce company, owner of the Taobao and Tmall marketplaces and of the country's biggest cloud business. Its New York-listed share is the one most foreign investors use to take a view on Chinese consumers and tech.
stocks:BABA.recent: The trough came the day Alibaba sued the Pentagon, denying any link to the Chinese military after being classified as a Chinese military affiliate. The recovery followed word that Apple's AI in China runs on Alibaba's Qwen models, and the launch in Hangzhou of N1 Pro glasses that verify payments by iris scan.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon Leo neared launch as the company stepped up satellite production, and Amazon weighed spending $7 billion on Decart, an AI startup Anthropic walked away from after offering $6 billion. It also reshuffled Alexa leadership after a high-end tablet release. None of it lines up with when the share turned.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's presidential election by a margin of four to eight percentage points. It prices how close the race is, not just who wins.
poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.recent: The fortnight's reporting on the race centred on Meta: researchers logged over 1,000 restrictions on political content, and the company admitted its AI generated images favouring Flávio Bolsonaro. Neither story accounts for the price of this margin band.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile lifted the shares and knocked Verizon and AT&T. Within a week Kyiv accused SpaceX of throttling Ukraine's Starlink terminals on fast-moving drones, and Musk blamed Washington. In New Delhi, Starlink holds a licence but still cannot sell service.

stocks:1211.HK.standing: The Shenzhen carmaker that builds only battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles and makes its own batteries. Its price cuts set the pace of China's car market, and its exports draw tariffs abroad.
stocks:1211.HK.recent: BYD said it will own 18 car-carrier ships by 2029, up from 8, because a shortage of vessels and war-driven freight costs, with Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb disrupted, are holding back its exports. Nothing in the reporting accounts for the fall in the shares.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.recent: The fortnight's prediction-market news concerned the markets themselves, not the midterms: 39 states and 145 tribal nations urged the Supreme Court to review them, and Kalshi's CEO said state-led oversight would push them out. None of it accounts for the price.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, the world's largest crude producer, listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh since 2019. The state keeps almost all of it, so the small float trades on oil prices and the dividend.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: The war with Yemen's Houthis reached the company itself: a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, and the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, Iran's state agency Mehr reported. Saudi Arabia also unexpectedly cut its oil prices to Asia. None of it accounts for the share's small drift.

stocks:COIN.standing: The largest US cryptocurrency exchange, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from trading fees and the interest on USDC stablecoin reserves, so its shares rise and fall with crypto prices and trading volume.
stocks:COIN.recent: The fortnight's stories about Coinbase itself were its call, as custodian of about 5% of all bitcoin, to start a quantum-resistant migration now, and its part alongside Binance in a West Africa scam sweep. Neither accounts for the share price.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The decline followed figures on China's AI chip market showing Huawei had shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months, taking share from Nvidia in a market where it once sold most of the chips.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu heads the government formed after Israel's next election. The premiership needs a 61-seat Knesset majority, so coalition arithmetic moves it as much as votes do.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Ahead of the legislative elections, Trump endorsed Netanyahu, former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar sued him for 3 million shekels in defamation over October 7, and the opposition called his new security doctrine "empty slogans". None of it accounts for the path of the price.

stocks:T.standing: One of the three national US mobile networks, alongside Verizon and T-Mobile, and a large fibre broadband provider. A heavy debt load and a long-paid dividend make it a stock held mainly for income.
stocks:T.recent: The sharpest fall came when SpaceX struck a nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile, bringing a satellite operator into the mobile market. AT&T and Verizon each dropped 7% on the news. Days later AT&T agreed to sell its Mexican business, 24.7 million subscribers, for $2 billion, pulling back to its home market.

stocks:TLEVISACPO.MX.standing: Mexico's largest broadcaster, listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange, which also runs the izzi cable and broadband network and Sky satellite TV. Its share tracks Mexican household spending on pay TV and connectivity.
stocks:TLEVISACPO.MX.recent: Televisa agreed to pay $2 billion for AT&T's Mexican business and its 24.7 million subscribers, which turns a cable and broadband company into a mobile operator as well. The deal came at the end of the window, and nothing in the input explains the earlier swings in the share.

wiki-china.standing: The daily count of readers of Wikipedia's article on China, the world's second-largest economy and its largest exporter. It shows how often the country's affairs send a general audience to look it up.
wiki-china.recent: The economy grew 4.5% year on year in the third quarter and retail sales rose 1.1%, more than double the forecast, while the PBOC said it would lend to funds, not just banks, to backstop the bond market. The EU planned to halve imports of Chinese hybrid cars. None of this falls on the early-month peak.

stocks:FFH.TO.standing: A Toronto holding company that owns property and casualty insurers and reinsurers around the world and invests their premiums, run by Prem Watsa in a value style. It has built large stakes in Indian companies.
stocks:FFH.TO.recent: Fairfax won 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore, India's largest privatisation, which puts the insurer's balance sheet in control of an Indian lender. The award came after the chart's last close, so none of the line reflects it, and nothing in the input explains the earlier moves.

stocks:PLTR.standing: Palantir Technologies, a US software company listed on Nasdaq, sells data-analysis platforms to defence ministries, intelligence agencies and large corporations. Government contracts make up a large share of its revenue.
stocks:PLTR.recent: France chose Chapsvision over another Palantir contract as Europe questioned its dependence on the company, while Louis Mosley warned Europe was 'missing the boat' on AI. HSBC's Islamic fund put $38m into the shares. None of it accounts for the price's path.

stocks:GFS.standing: A contract chipmaker that builds other companies' designs, specialising in older, cheaper process nodes used in cars, phones, radios and defence electronics. It is one of the few foundries headquartered in the US.
stocks:GFS.recent: Washington doubled its equity stake in GlobalFoundries to nearly 8% and will partner with it on a new fab at Malta, New York, a step from CHIPS Act grants to outright ownership. The deal came after this chart's last close, so it does not account for the rise shown here.

stocks:RELIANCE.NS.standing: India's most valuable listed company, a Mumbai conglomerate that runs the Jamnagar refining complex alongside Jio telecoms and India's biggest retail chain. Its size makes it a swing stock for the whole Indian market.
stocks:RELIANCE.NS.recent: Reliance is floating Jio Platforms, its telecom arm, in what it priced as India's largest offering, seeking up to ₹30,213 crore; the $3.2 billion sale drew nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand, sovereign funds among the bidders. Separately, Reliance answered Musk over Starlink, saying its own satellite service awaits the same clearances.

stocks:ACN.standing: One of the world's largest consulting and IT-services firms, incorporated in Ireland and listed in New York. Its shares track how much corporations spend on outsourcing, and lately on help adopting AI.
stocks:ACN.recent: The one story about Accenture's own business was a cost cut: staff who had spent up to $1,000 a month on Claude were capped at $29, a firm that sells AI transformation to clients now rationing it for its own workers. It landed at the end of the rise, which began in late September, and does not account for it.

stocks:NESN.SW.standing: The world's largest packaged-food company, based in Vevey, Switzerland, selling Nescafé, Maggi, Purina and infant formula almost everywhere. A heavyweight of the Swiss SMI, its share moves with coffee, cocoa and dairy costs.

stocks:BA.L.standing: Britain's largest defence company, building warships, nuclear submarines, combat aircraft and munitions, with a large US arm. Its shares move on NATO governments' defence budgets and the export orders they approve.
stocks:BA.L.recent: A cyberattack on BAE Systems, working as a contractor for the US courts, halted all notices for US bankruptcy courts. The attack was reported in Washington after the slide had already happened, and nothing else in the input explains the price.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares in Tesla, the US maker of electric cars and grid batteries, listed on Nasdaq. Its valuation rests more on bets about self-driving cars and robots than on the cars it sells today, so it moves on Elon Musk's promises.
stocks:TSLA.recent: Tesla's push into India stalled alongside Starlink's, and the new Roadster was unveiled only after the last close shown here. Musk's Paxton donation and Tesla blocking a federal tracker are not about its business, and nothing in the input accounts for the share price.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Apple's shares, traded on the Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from the iPhone, and its weight as one of the world's most valuable companies means its moves carry the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices with it.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo opened and were backordered until 2027 within a day, three days after Apple introduced HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home. The same day Apple Intelligence entered China in beta, running on Alibaba's Qwen models.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The first cryptocurrency, a fixed-supply digital currency run on a public ledger with no central issuer, launched in 2009. Its price sets the tone for the whole crypto market, and funds, banks and listed companies now hold it.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The fortnight's bitcoin news was about quantum computing: Google said Willow cut magic-state errors about 40-fold, 6.4 million bitcoin have public keys already exposed, and Coinbase urged a quantum-resistant fix. MSCI also moved to eject treasury firms such as Strategy and Metaplanet. None of it accounts for the early-October peak.

stocks:MSTR.standing: A Nasdaq-listed software company that became the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, funding its purchases by selling new shares and debt. Its stock trades as a leveraged bet on the bitcoin price.
